steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Hello, Master Wei.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Take a seat.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Officer Swire, there is something we must discuss.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Oh? Well, that's a new one. We've never had a discussion, just the two of us, have we?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You might want to get used to it, then.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: So Officer Ch'en isn't coming back?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: No, she isn't.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: There are a lot of superintendents in the L.G.D. Why me? The things Officer Ch'en did, I might not...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You needn't do what 'Officer Ch'en did.' She was never the ideal choice to lead the Special Inspection Unit.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Master Wei? Just because Officer Ch'en is gone doesn't mean you're free to speak ill of her.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I don't mean to speak ill. However, Officer Ch'en's strongest merit is her sense of justice, and that is also her greatest weakness. Her position called for more than a sense of justice.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Did it? Hm... Let me think... What else could you expect from me?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Good relationships stakeholding factions? A talent for command? A new face from the next generation? A bad relationship with Officer Ch'en? You wouldn't be after my family, right?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You speak your mind, Swire.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I've never been one to beat around the bush. I'm not my grandfather, Master Wei.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: And here I thought you'd avoid the word 'Grandfather.'

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: There was a time when I did, though I've since gotten used to it. He casts a long shadow in the L.G.D., and there's no running from the name 'Adams Schwire' as long as I live here.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hah... I can't recall hearing an ordinary Lungmenite say his name. Perhaps it's not Lungmen that can't run from it, Officer Swire. It's you who can't escape the name.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Let's cut to the chase, Master Wei.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I know the current L.G.D. Commissioner is one of his lackeys, no matter how solid his relationship with you. I also know that the longer my grandfather stays in his sickbed, the more uncertain things get.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: My family has had its differences with you, even before my grandfather got sick, but we always knew that the Corporate Union and Lungmen should and must coexist.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Now that my grandfather has been bedridden for fourteen years and counting, though, things have gotten far too chaotic and stupid with the men supposed to carry out his will.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: If they continue this way, what will become of the relationship between the Schwires and Lungmen by the time he finally shuffles off his mortal coil? This is a problem you have to face, Master Wei, just as the L.G.D. must.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And maybe... It's one that I have to face too.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Am I right?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I think I just saw Adams in you, young lady.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: That's a provocation, Master Wei. I resent the idea that anyone would see a single trace of him in me.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: My apologies. It was not my intention to provoke.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Fair enough. It seems to me you might have a slight misunderstanding about the relationships in my family... I'm not sure exactly how you think we get along with each other.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: If you don't want to go into the details, forget I ever said anything.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No... It's alright.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I've been thinking I might have to talk to you about this sooner or later, if I ended up taking over for Ch'en.

steps.name: Young Swire
steps.text: Waaaahhh...

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Shh, shh... Beatrix, don't cry...

steps.name: Young Swire
steps.text: *Whimpers*... But Daddy... They were mean to me...

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Shh... Grandpa is still home. Don't disturb him...

steps.name: Young Swire
steps.text: *Waaahhh... Uwargh-wah-hh!

steps.name: Father
steps.text: I told you to stop crying! You don't want to disturb him!
A loud slap.

steps.name: Adams Schwire's Secretary
steps.text: Is something the matter? Master Schwire said he heard a commotion.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: No, not at all. I was just taking Beatrix! Awfully, terribly sorry, sir. She did not mean to disturb Father.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Childhood memories tend to be blurry, and they say that if you have one that's particularly clear, it must've had a profound impact on your personality.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: So then, if I remember this so vividly even now, does that mean it was the first time I truly came to 'know' my grandfather?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: If my memory serves me right, your father is Adams's oldest son, and your grandfather had high hopes for him in his younger years... Hoh... Indeed, that's just like Adams.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: It doesn't seem like you grew up in the same kind of environment he did, though.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: My parents moved out of the place many years ago, after all. I could count the number of times I've met my grandfather on one hand. When he wasn't around, my parents treated me well.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Though... in another sense... I have always lived in his shadow.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: 'Don't do that, Grandpa said.' 'Don't play with them. Grandpa wouldn't like it.' —All the things I wasn't allowed to do when I was little, they were all because of 'Grandpa's wishes.'

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: —Not that I ever listened to him much.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I cried, I got angry. I even asked, 'Why am I not allowed, just because Grandpa wouldn't be happy about it?' My parents were never able to give me a reason, but I could tell. They were much more afraid of him than I ever was.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: They weren't even trying to get on my grandfather's good side. They were just afraid of making him angry.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: In the end, my grandfather was the thing I feared most at the time. He was like... just like a monster that ends up killing the heroes in a B movie.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Who would show their child something like that?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I saw one once, and it kept me up all night. When I told my parents, '*Sobs* That ghost's scarier than Grandpa—' I got an earful from my father.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Then, I started to think: Oh, so Grandpa's actually scarier.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: It doesn't sound so bad just listening to the story, does it? Believe me, though. It wasn't easy to live through. There was a time when I thought of 'angering Grandfather' as the red line that could never be crossed.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But some time after that...

steps.name: Nameless Lungmen Policeman
steps.text: Over here!

steps.name: Nameless Lungmen Policeman
steps.text: The hostage is safe! Move in!

steps.name: Nameless Lungmen Policeman
steps.text: Little girl, are you okay?

steps.name: Lungmen Policeman
steps.text: Contact! It's the kidnapper! Requesting backup!

steps.name: Nameless Lungmen Policeman
steps.text: 10-4! I'll bring the girl out first!

steps.name: Young Swire
steps.text: Yes... I'm okay.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Master Wei, I'm sure you've figured out by now that it was then I decided to become a police officer. I'm sure you've also figured out that...
Another loud slap.

steps.name: Young Swire
steps.text: Daddy...?

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Sorry, Beatrix, I should not have slapped you, but... How could you? You stand to inherit everything! How could you say you want to join the police?

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Father... Father will be furious when he finds out about this! You must abandon this idea!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I was actually baffled. You see, my cousin had just told me a few months prior that he was the first in line to take over.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But when he said it, something felt off to me.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: The heir to the Schwire family fortune... Shouldn't that be...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Correct, neither me nor my cousin. It should have been my father.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: This is one of those questions that I could never wrap my head around when I was a kid, and then one day, after I'd grown up, I suddenly realized that it couldn't have been any simpler.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: —Of course, my father didn't want to take over, and my grandfather never thought of him as a successor.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: He's always called me the heir to the Schwires. Maybe that's his honest belief, but looking back...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: He was probably just thinking something like: 'As long it's not me, it doesn't matter who it is.'

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: At the time, I still trusted my father, though. Or maybe I should say... even if they have their doubts, there aren't a lot of kids out there who don't trust their parents.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I was scared. I kept hoping I could avoid becoming the heir.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: So that's why...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I still remember the time we first met.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Ha... That's another one of my childhood traumas.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: How's Father? Is he well?

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I'm afraid... Mr. Schwire's outlook isn't very optimistic.

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Master Wei, I didn't expect you to visit today... To what do we owe the pleasure?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: My old friend is sick, so I'm here to visit. Doctor, please continue.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: His current situation isn't life threatening, but I'm afraid it'll be difficult for him to ever leave his bed again.

steps.name: Young Swire
steps.text: Pfffheh.

steps.name: Uncle
steps.text: Beatrix? What's so funny?!

steps.name: Aunt
steps.text: This... This is unbelievable!

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Sorry... Beatrix, apologize! I'm sorry, Master Wei for my daughter's behavior... Beatrix!

steps.name: Adams Schwire
steps.text: (Quietly) Hoh...

steps.name: Father
steps.text: Father, you're awake?!

steps.name: Adams Swire
steps.text: (Quietly) My unseemly granddaughter... She's a brave one, but she doesn't mince words.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Looking back, that was the only praise I ever got from my grandfather. At the time, I didn't even realize what he meant by it. I could only feel... chills, running down my spine.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I've heard your family still ostracizes you because of that.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Right, they always say I'm an ungrateful, unfilial daughter. Not that I can really disagree with them.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I guess Grandfather probably didn't mind that I was looking forward to his death, though. He just thought the way I couldn't hold back my laugh was unreasonable and could put him in a difficult position.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: —I was only twelve! Did he really expect me to hide my feelings about everything?!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You're beginning to put yourself in his shoes.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Yes, you're right. I had a terrible time after that. Every so often, someone would bring it up.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: A year or two later, though, I suddenly realized something.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: By then, my grandfather was already pretty quiet on his sickbed... He wasn't even awake much, actually. Nevertheless, I still lived in his shadow.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Actually, even before that, I rarely saw him actually giving orders.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: So how did he cast that shadow anyway? Did it come from my grandfather? From my father, my relatives? Or was it actually cast... by my own heart?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: He barely said a word the year after he was bedridden. How come nobody dared to stand up against him? He didn't actually hold much power, but no one resisted him. Why?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Forgive me, Officer Swire... but you don't seem like the type to ponder these matters at age thirteen or so.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Alright, alright! I'm just organizing all the doubts I had at the time! I'm looking back with the wisdom of age, okay?!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: To tell you the truth, I was only muddling along back then. I didn't think, much less notice what was really on my mind.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: If it wasn't for the cop who saved me, my guess is I would probably be just another loafing, good-for-nothing rich kid.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I still have the badge he dropped during the kidnapping case. If I ever find him, I'd really like to give him a proper thank you...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: If you ask me, becoming a superintendent is the best way to show your appreciation.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I suppose so.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Anyway, I went to Victoria for school, basically because I was trying to get away from Lungmen.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I thought that, by going to Victoria, I could finally escape my grandfather's shadow. Boy, was I wrong.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I should've known... The Schwires have far more assets in Victoria than Lungmen.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Those businesses in Victoria had long tried to shake off Adams's control, even before then.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Right, that's why, by going to Victoria, I actually managed to suss out my grandfather's position a little. It was like I finally found some of the answers to all the doubts that had been lingering in my mind.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I guess... there are a lot of ways to grasp power, but there is only one way to maintain that power, and that's to be right.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: My grandfather could buy dignity with his power, but when he lost the ability to use that power, no one dared to turn on him, and there's only one reason why that is: He's always right.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Officer Swire, I thought you were here to swear your allegiance, until you said that.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And that's exactly why I am here! Are him being right and me opposing him somehow mutually exclusive?!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Oh? So you'll betray your family?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Master Wei! Please, enough teasing already!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: —I am absolutely not teasing.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: My grandfather has done a lot right, there's no arguing that. But sometimes, there's more than one 'right' in this world.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What's right for the Schwires isn't necessarily what's right for Lungmen, what was right before isn't necessarily the right way forward, and what used to be right for my grandfather definitely isn't going to be right for me.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: The thought of betraying my family has never crossed my mind. And the idea of betraying Lungmen is even crazier, because I won't ever betray my badge.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: That's my answer, Master Wei. I'll leave it there for now.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Heh... You can keep going.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Where was I...?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Oh, I learned a little about my family's past during secondary school, and that was when I realized how my grandfather had planned everything so carefully when he moved the family business out of Victoria.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: He predicted Victoria's troubles and fissures over forty years ago. He knew Victoria's fall was coming even at the height of its prosperity.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And then, even though nobody understood his decision, he stubbornly pressed forward until history finally proved him right.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And also... fine, I'll stop singing his praises. I'm sure you know more about his exploits than I do anyway.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Anyway, I'd be lying if I said I never wavered during this whole process. Though I came to understand that all this... didn't actually make me fear him any more.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: In fact, the more I learned about his achievements... the weaker my fear became.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: All because I couldn't figure out the source of my fear.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Back when I didn't understand anything, my grandfather cast a dark shadow, shrouding even the sky itself. The depth of his terror was limited only by my imagination.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But when I finally understood the source of his power, he was only as terrifying as the bounds of reality. I know why there is no standing up to him, and that's how...

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: That's how I figured out how to stand up to him.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: And that's that... but I didn't actually mean to backstab anyone, you know?!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: They call me 'unseemly' day in and day out, like everything I do is some kind of dig at them. What's that about?!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: That hotheadedness runs in your family. Surely you know that?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Of course I do, and that just makes me all the more pissed! Why do I have to take over the family business and have them prickling at me day after day? What's wrong with the L.G.D.?!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I've long heard rumors of the L.G.D. Officer Swire with her booming voice that echoes loud and clear. It seems the rumors are true.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Ahem. Anyway, I figured at the time... running away won't solve anything.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: If I kept running away, then even if I managed to become a cop, I might still shudder in fear every time my thoughts turned to my grandfather.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What's more, he'd see me running. And that would only lend more credence to his idea that I'm an unseemly granddaughter.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: No, thank you.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: And that is why, starting your third year of university, you began to take on work in the family business—even if it was in direct opposition to your parents' wishes.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Right... Now that you mention it, they grumbled about that for quite a long while. No matter. Who cares what they think?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: In 1092, the Schwire Group's Lungmen headquarters issued an order to its real estate officer in northern Victoria to sell off some of their properties there.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: The director refused the order and submitted a report describing why the order was not feasible.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Working through a classmate, you got your hands on certain internal data from the dukedom in question and pointed out errors in the report. That was the first time you meddled in your family's business.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: However, the officer very quickly submitted a second report and plugged all the holes you found.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: In the end, the plan to sell off the properties did not succeed.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: In 1094, you came back to Lungmen, and while you were interning at one of your family's companies, you found out a director trying to get the Corporate Union and Lungmen to turn on each other.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: And you picked a fight during a meeting.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: In the end, the director's plan was foiled, and the individual was relieved of duty. However, you also had to leave the Schwire Group.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: 1095. That was your first year with the L.G.D. The Lungmen Trade Union held a strike over a wage dispute. The Corporate Union asked the L.G.D. to end the strike.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: In private, you arranged for a meeting between the Trade Unionists and the Corporate Union, though it fell apart. You couldn't stop the strike, and you ended up in a huge row with the Commissioner.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Following that, during a Schwire family meeting, your cousin accused you of damaging the Corporate Union's profits, though you fought back, and you did not find yourself more ostracized.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Why are you recounting my life story, Master Wei?! I know I didn't accomplish much during those few years, but growth happens over time!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Look at how much I've done lately!

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: I'm not trying to make fun of you, Officer Swire.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Do you remember what you said earlier? You asked me what more I expect from you.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You're wrong to question yourself. This is what I expect to see in you. What the L.G.D. looks to uphold is not justice.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You've been working to accomplish everything I want out of the L.G.D. You will experience even more failures than you did those few years, but just as you've never given up before, you won't give up now.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Master Wei... I'm just thinking... whether I can accomplish the task at hand isn't actually that important.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: What matters is this is the only way I can find courage, and win the right to choose my own path.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I think I have a pretty good idea of what my grandfather thinks of me being a cop—'You don't have what it takes to devour the L.G.D., so why are you even doing this?'

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: —Maybe something like that? I don't really care anymore, though... Definitely. I don't care. Who cares what he thinks?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: You don't care? How did you manage such a flawless impression him, though?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Oh... I mean, I've been fixated on this since I was a kid. I can't completely not care!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: I'm sure you can tell. In recounting my childhood to you, I'm pledging my loyalty.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: But now I know. You've seen what I've done these past four years... No, maybe you've been keeping an eye on me since even before that.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: My actions thus far say much more about my position and how I feel than mere words. And when I say that, I guess it makes this conversation seem kind of meaningless.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Not necessarily... It's true that I used to see Adams in you.

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Not that you look anything like him.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Hmm... Actually, even now, I can't say for sure he never influenced me. After all, I know in my heart that I actually do care what he thinks.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: That said... Master Wei, are you willing to have a little faith in me?

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Wei Yenwu
steps.text: It's just as you said. Actions speak louder than words.

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Well, then... You won't be disappointed.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hey, I heard the news. Congratulations on your promotion, Missy.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer A
steps.text: Congrats! Dinner's on you tonight, Missy!

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Fine, whatever! What happened to all your cases? What are you all faffing about for? Get back to work!

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer B
steps.text: No way, Missy! Not even officially on the job yet, and you're already terrorizing us with your newfound power?

steps.name: Swire
steps.text: Enough with the glib tongue! To your cases! Everything's on me tonight!

a.text: It's true. I'm not sure whether my grandfather's shadow is still influencing my decisions.

Sometimes, I manage to break free. Other times, I'm pulled back toward him. Resistance is a different, vicious cycle. Standing up to my fears is not an insult to him. It's a means to forget—though I will never forget my grandfather's gaze or his will.
Even so, I'm confident I can find my own way forward.
After all, even if I never shake free of his influence, the warmth this badge brings me has nothing to do with him. My colleagues' laughter has nothing to do with him.
—Lungmen's future has nothing to do with him.
